key_catalyst: Operational U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz with 20% cargo toll and third night of strikes, driving Brent up ~9% above $85
reasoning: The Hormuz situation has materially escalated from yesterday's 'closure fears' to an operational U.S. blockade with a 20% cargo toll, a third night of strikes, and oil spiking ~9% overnight — a worse shock than the +4.3% oil move that drove QQQ -1.90% on 2026-07-13. The +0.95% pre-market bounce rests entirely on hope for a soft backward-looking CPI print, while the oil shock and ~41-50% July rate-hike odds directly undermine forward disinflation and long-duration tech valuations; Warsh's testimony today adds hawkish tail risk. The 2026-07-10 session showed this market prematurely priced the conflict as 'contained' before the 07-13 selloff, and today's CPI-driven complacency looks like the same underreaction pattern.
